entries.title: The United States’ Accelerating Memory Chip Crunch: Implications for Tech and AI Leadership
entries.description: The rapid expansion of AI data centers is creating adverse effects across the memory chip ecosystem. As memory suppliers shift toward high-bandwidth memory, shortages of conventional RAM are raising costs for consumer electronics and fueling calls for government action.

entries.title: A Global Forced Labor Import Regime Is Emerging—Can It Work?
entries.description: USTR announced sweeping tariffs across 60 economies to address unfair trade practices related to the importation of forced labor-made goods. This presents significant opportunities for promoting workers' rights as well as potentially dire risks to those same rights.

entries.title: Six Reasons Why the United States Is Low on Munitions
entries.description: The Iran war has exacerbated the Pentagon’s shortage of key munitions, but it is not the only cause. There are also longstanding strategic, operational, and institutional reasons.

entries.title: Build, Not Buy: The Semiconductor Lesson that Indian AI Experts Must Learn
entries.description: As AI grows more sophisticated, as the supply chains that power it become more contested, and as access to frontier models becomes geopolitically charged, India must begin to ask a different set of questions. Not what applications it can build on someone else’s infrastructure but what the world needs.

entries.title: "I Don’t Think Trump Wants to Pull America Out of NATO"
entries.description: Does Donald Trump want to redraw the map of the world? Historian and geopolitical thinker Stephen Wertheim tries to parse the logic behind current American foreign policy
